Container.Name: the-desk
Container.Overview: The Desk — the morning order-sizing worksheet. Sizes each recurring buy from where a position's 30-day average sits in its 52-week range (top third 1x, middle 2x, bottom third 3x of a per-position daily base), and shows accounts, a taxable-lot LTCG exit ladder, the Monte Carlo trend against the retirement band, and the rules registry. Every displayed number traces to the payload plus a rule id; the tool never decides — all orders are hand-placed. IT SHIPS EMPTY: a first boot shows an empty wallet, which is correct rather than a misconfiguration — there is no sample data in the image and nothing is ever substituted for data you have not imported. HOW HOLDINGS GET IN: drop a custodian CSV into the inbox subdirectory of the Data path and it is read within a few minutes, then moved into inbox/imported or inbox/rejected beside it so nothing is ever consumed silently. Fidelity's Portfolio Positions export is the format understood today; a row that cannot be read is quarantined with its reason and the dashboard says so rather than importing part of a file quietly. There is deliberately NO upload button: the dashboard has no authentication, and an unauthenticated route that writes to your wallet is one a browser on your LAN can be made to submit to. Tax lots are not present in a positions export and are not invented from one, so the LTCG ladder stays empty until a file that carries them can be ingested. IMPORTANT: the Data path (/data) now holds the wallet itself — accounts, positions, tax lots and cash flow, in a SQLite store — as well as the notifier's bookkeeping; losing that volume loses the wallet, so put it on a pool and back it up. Tape supplies market data only: set TAPE_BASE_URL, then set a Tape credential from the container's console - preferred: `python -m app.settings set TAPE_CLIENT_ID` and `python -m app.settings set TAPE_CLIENT_SECRET`; or the legacy shared key, `python -m app.settings set TAPE_API_KEY` - the same way the chat-client token below is set; there is no template field for any of the three, and each takes effect on the next request with no restart. Without Tape the wallet still renders and nothing can be sized, and the page says exactly that. READING IT FROM A CHAT CLIENT: two token-gated, read-only routes - the data API (/api/v1/data, the page's own document) and an MCP endpoint (/mcp) with four tools: worksheet, accounts, lots, review - open once a bearer token is set. There is no template field for it: from the container's console run `python -m app.settings set DESK_API_TOKEN` and type the value at the hidden prompt; it is kept in the wallet store on the Data path and takes effect on the next request without a restart. Leave it unset and both routes stay closed; either way nothing reachable through them can place an order. NOTIFICATIONS: exactly two events — a band tier change, and a lot entering the 30-day LTCG window — and every ping is also recorded on the page under SINCE LAST LOOK, so nothing is lost if a channel is down. There are no ntfy or email settings on this template: alerting is configured once for the whole fleet in a shared file (configs/alerting.env under the Shared alerting root), which is why moving the inbox or re-pointing a topic is one edit rather than one per container — see github.com/sdr-ventures/kw-common/blob/main/docs/alerting-setup.md. READ THIS BEFORE THE FIRST APPLY: this container REFUSES TO START if that file is missing, unreadable, incomplete, still carries a CHANGE-ME placeholder, or names an ntfy topic as a bare word rather than a full https URL. That is deliberate — a service that cannot alert must not come up pretending it can — and the container log names which one it was. Set the Shared alerting root and DEPLOY_ENV (prod or dev) and the first boot sends one confirmation message to prove the channel works; it is not repeated on later boots unless the shared file changes.
Container.Description: The Desk — daily order-sizing worksheet and investment-monitoring dashboard (Flask).

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: THE WALLET LIVES HERE - back it up. Holds desk.sqlite3 (your accounts, positions, tax lots and cash flow - everything the dashboard is built from - and the settings table, including the chat-client API token and any Tape credential you set from the console, so a copy of this volume carries those too) plus notifier-state.json (which tier each symbol was last seen at, and which LTCG crossings have already pinged) and the inbox/ directory you drop statements into (with imported/ and rejected/ beneath it, holding every file the container has processed). Losing this volume loses the wallet, recoverable only by importing the statements again; losing just the notifier state costs one pass with no TIER change badges and possibly one repeated LTCG ping. Through v0.2.0 this held only the bookkeeping and was cheap to lose - that is no longer true. REQUIRED - an absolute path on a POOL.

Config.Name: Backups
Config.Description: Where the wallet backup lands. REQUIRED: WITHOUT this mount a backup written to any in-container path is destroyed by the next image update, with nothing to say so at the time. Set an absolute path on a POOL DIFFERENT from the one holding the Data mount above, so one pool failure cannot take both the wallet and its only backup.

Config.Name: TAPE_BASE_URL
Config.Description: Base URL of the Tape API, e.g. https://tape.example.com (no trailing path). Needed for PRICES, which is all Tape supplies - your holdings come from the local store. Without it the container starts, serves the page and shows what you hold; no position can be sized, and the page names the variables to set rather than going blank.

Config.Name: Shared alerting root
Config.Description: REQUIRED. The host directory holding configs/alerting.env - the ONE file every Keystone container reads for its alerting settings. Mounted READ-ONLY: this container never writes to it. Create the directory, fetch the annotated template into configs/alerting.env, restrict it (it holds an SMTP password) and fill it in BEFORE you Apply - a missing or unfilled file stops this container from starting, on purpose. WATCH THE FILE PERMISSIONS, THIS IS THE STEP THAT BITES: this container runs as uid 99, gid 100 (nobody:users) - not as you - so a file left mode 600 owned by the account that downloaded it is unreadable to the service, which then refuses to boot with a message about a file that is plainly sitting right there. 99:100 is what Unraid gives appdata written over SMB, which is why those numbers were chosen - but DO NOT ASSUME it is already right: creating the file from a root shell gives root:root, and chmod 600 then locks uid 99 out. After restricting it, run either 'chown 99:100 configs/alerting.env' with mode 600, or 'chgrp 100 configs/alerting.env' with mode 640 - the second keeps it readable to your own account too, which is handier while you are still editing it. Full instructions: github.com/sdr-ventures/kw-common/blob/main/docs/alerting-setup.md

Config.Name: DEPLOY_ENV
Config.Description: REQUIRED - type prod or dev. It selects which ntfy topic from the shared file this container publishes to (NTFY_URL_PROD or NTFY_URL_DEV) and which keys must be present. DELIBERATELY BLANK: a default here would silently put a dev deployment on the prod topic, and the symptom of that is an incident that paged the wrong place. Case does not matter.

Config.Name: TZ
Config.Description: Container timezone. Drives the notification cron below and the dates written into events. Set it to your own zone or the evening pass will fire at the wrong hour.

Config.Name: DESK_NOTIFY_CRON
Config.Description: When to run the NOTIFICATION pass, as a 5-field cron in the container's TZ. This does NOT feed the dashboard — the page is live and never waits on it. It exists because a tier CHANGE is only visible to something that was awake to see the previous tier. Default 17:30 Mon-Fri, after the close. A missed pass is not chased; the next one picks up whatever moved. USE NAMED DAYS (mon-fri), never numbers: the scheduler counts 0 as Monday, so a crontab-style 1-5 fires Tue-Sat — dropping Monday and adding a day with no close.

Config.Name: DESK_NOTIFY_ON_BOOT
Config.Description: Also run the notification pass at container start. Leave true unless you are debugging; it seeds the tier baseline so the first scheduled pass has something to compare against. It does not affect what the dashboard displays.

Config.Name: DESK_INTAKE_INTERVAL_MIN
Config.Description: How often, in minutes, to look in the Data path's inbox/ directory for a dropped statement. Also runs once at container start, so a file put there before a restart is read immediately rather than after a full interval. Set to 0 to disable the scan entirely if you would rather import by hand. This has nothing to do with prices - intake works with no Tape credentials set at all, which is the state a first install is in.

Config.Name: DESK_INTAKE_SETTLE_SECONDS
Config.Description: A file whose modified time is younger than this many seconds is left alone for a later scan instead of being read now - a safety net against reading a statement while it is still being copied onto this share. Default 0 (off), because how long a copy takes is specific to how you get files here; set it to a few seconds more than that.

Config.Name: DESK_STALE_AMBER_HOURS
Config.Description: rule stale-1: price age at which the banner turns amber (AGING). Sizes are still shown.

Config.Name: DESK_STALE_RED_HOURS
Config.Description: rule stale-1: price age at which the banner turns red (STALE) and every computed buy size is WITHHELD — no verdict from stale data. Must be greater than the amber threshold.

Config.Name: DESK_LOG_LEVEL
Config.Description: INFO (default) or DEBUG. Credentials are never logged at any level.
